note: Every benchmark gao is judged on, and every benchmark the corpus is checked against before a release. It only grows. A benchmark comes off this file when it stops existing, not when it comes back contaminated. A revision here is the object id its home answers with, because a version number is a name and the files behind a name can be reuploaded. Twelve of these are pinned and twelve are not, and each of the twelve that is not says what it is waiting for.

benchmarks.name: vmlu
benchmarks.source: ZaloAI-Jaist/VMLU, the public evaluation split
benchmarks.note: Vietnamese multitask knowledge across 58 subjects, and the primary gate. Items are the question and all of the options, without the answer key, because a page that reproduces a question and its options is the leak and a page that lists answer letters is not.

benchmarks.name: vimmrc
benchmarks.source: the UIT NLP group's own copy of ViMMRC 2.0 on the Hub, test split
benchmarks.note: Reading comprehension over school texts. Items are the passage and the questions. The passages are published Vietnamese schoolbook material, so overlap here is expected and says more about the source than about the pipeline. Only 2.0 is pinned, because 1.0 exists on the Hub in third party copies alone.

benchmarks.name: uit-viquad
benchmarks.pending: UIT-ViQuAD 2.0 is handed out on request by the UIT NLP group and every copy on the Hub is somebody else's upload. Pinning one of those would pin the upload rather than the benchmark, which is a weaker claim than a release note makes. This waits for an address the authors answer for.
benchmarks.source: UIT NLP group, UIT-ViQuAD 2.0
benchmarks.note: Extractive QA with unanswerable questions. Items are the context paragraph and the questions. The contexts are drawn from Vietnamese Wikipedia, which is in the corpus, so this one is expected to come back contaminated and the useful number is how much of it.

benchmarks.name: vinli
benchmarks.pending: ViNLI has no copy published by its authors. What is on the Hub under the name is derived splits built for training sentence embedding models, and a derived split is a different set of items with a different licence behind it.
benchmarks.source: UIT NLP group, ViNLI test split
benchmarks.note: Natural language inference. Items are the premise and the hypothesis as one text, because either alone is short enough to be an ordinary Vietnamese sentence.

benchmarks.name: uit-vsfc
benchmarks.source: the UIT NLP group's own copy of UIT-VSFC on the Hub, test split
benchmarks.note: Student feedback sentiment. Items are the feedback sentences. Many are shorter than the window and produce no grams at all, which is reported rather than hidden.

benchmarks.name: visfd
benchmarks.source: the first author's repository, test split
benchmarks.note: Aspect based sentiment over smartphone reviews. Items are the review text, which is the kind of text a review aggregator republishes, so this one is worth watching.

benchmarks.name: vihsd
benchmarks.source: the UIT NLP group's own copy of UIT-ViHSD on the Hub, test split
benchmarks.note: Hate speech detection. Items are the comments. They came off social media and they are short, so both a low gram yield and real overlap are plausible.

benchmarks.name: victsd
benchmarks.source: the first author's copy on the Hub, test split
benchmarks.note: Constructive and toxic speech detection over news comments.

benchmarks.name: vlsp
benchmarks.pending: VLSP is a suite and the roster carries it as one row. There is a separate evaluation set per year and per task, so there is no single revision to pin, and the row has to be split before there is one. This is the same simplification the note calls out, seen from the pinning side.
benchmarks.source: VLSP shared task evaluation sets, per year and per task
benchmarks.note: NER, parsing, machine translation and summarization. This is a suite rather than one benchmark and the roster carries it as one row, which is a simplification that has to end before the suite is used as a gate.

benchmarks.name: phomt
benchmarks.source: VinAI Research's own copy of PhoMT on the Hub, test split
benchmarks.note: Vietnamese and English translation with human quality references. Items are the Vietnamese side. The English side belongs in the check too and needs an English key rather than this one.

benchmarks.name: mmlu-vi
benchmarks.source: the Vietnamese config of m_mmlu, which is what lm-evaluation-harness v0.4.12 runs as m_mmlu_vi
benchmarks.note: Reported, never a gate. A clean result here is weak evidence: an item that reached the corpus through a different translation of the same English source shares no window with this one.

benchmarks.name: gsm8k-vi
benchmarks.pending: There is no Vietnamese GSM8K to pin. MGSM, which is where lm-evaluation-harness keeps translated grade school arithmetic, covers eleven languages at v0.4.12 and Vietnamese is not one of them. This row names a benchmark that has to be found or built, not one that is waiting on an address.
benchmarks.source: no Vietnamese translation in the harness, see pending
benchmarks.note: Grade school arithmetic word problems. Items are the problem statements without the worked solutions.

benchmarks.name: math-vi
benchmarks.pending: There is no Vietnamese MATH to pin. The harness carries the Vietnamese subject splits of MMLU-ProX at v0.4.12, which include mathematics, and those are not this benchmark. Same as gsm8k-vi: the row has to be found or built before it can be pinned.
benchmarks.source: no Vietnamese translation in the harness, see pending
benchmarks.note: Competition mathematics. The problem statements carry a lot of notation, which survives the deduplication key poorly, so the gram yield per item is low and the check is weaker here than elsewhere.

benchmarks.name: arc-vi
benchmarks.source: the Vietnamese config of m_arc, which is what lm-evaluation-harness v0.4.12 runs as arc_vi
benchmarks.note: Science questions. Items are the question and the options.

benchmarks.name: hellaswag-vi
benchmarks.source: the Vietnamese config of m_hellaswag, which is what lm-evaluation-harness v0.4.12 runs as hellaswag_vi
benchmarks.note: Commonsense continuation. Items are the context and all four endings, because the wrong endings are machine written and are the part that could only have come from the benchmark.

benchmarks.name: winogrande-vi
benchmarks.pending: There is no Vietnamese Winogrande to pin. The okapi set in lm-evaluation-harness, which is where its translated multiple choice lives, carries ARC, HellaSwag, MMLU and TruthfulQA at v0.4.12 and not this one.
benchmarks.source: no Vietnamese translation in the harness, see pending
benchmarks.note: Pronoun resolution. The items are one sentence each and most of them are shorter than the window, so this benchmark is largely invisible to an n-gram check and the embedding check is the one that will find it.

benchmarks.name: humaneval
benchmarks.source: OpenAI's own copy on the Hub, prompts and tests
benchmarks.note: Code, so the text is English docstrings and Python. The deduplication key was built for Vietnamese prose and folds this text harder than it should, which makes the check here loose rather than tight.

benchmarks.name: mbpp
benchmarks.source: Google Research's own copy on the Hub, test split
benchmarks.note: Code. Same caveat as HumanEval.

benchmarks.name: vi-cloze
benchmarks.pending: Built by gao and not built yet. It gets a revision when the held out split exists and is written down somewhere that can be asked for one.
benchmarks.source: built by gao, doc 10 section 2.2
benchmarks.note: 20,000 ranking items built from held out gao-web. Overlap is not a finding here, it is the hold out failing, so one shared window drops the document.

benchmarks.name: vi-diacritic
benchmarks.pending: Built by gao and not built yet. It gets a revision when the held out split exists.
benchmarks.source: built by gao, doc 10 section 1.2
benchmarks.note: 5,000 sentences held out from gao-web with the tone marks stripped. Held out, so one shared window drops the document. The stripped side is not in the list because undiacriticized Vietnamese is a real register that the corpus is supposed to contain.

benchmarks.name: vi-needle
benchmarks.pending: Built by gao and not built yet. The haystacks come out of gao-legal and gao-pdf, so this one cannot be pinned before those two exist either.
benchmarks.source: built by gao, doc 10 section 1.2
benchmarks.note: Long context retrieval with haystacks drawn from gao-legal and gao-pdf. The haystacks are corpus text by construction, so the items are the needles and the questions rather than the haystacks.

benchmarks.name: vi-longdoc-qa
benchmarks.pending: Built by gao and not built yet. The questions are human written, so this one is waiting on people rather than on a run.
benchmarks.source: built by gao, doc 10 section 1.2
benchmarks.note: 2,000 human written questions over 400 long documents. Items are the questions. The documents stay in the corpus on purpose, because removing 400 statutes and theses to protect a benchmark would be the tail wagging the dog, and the questions are what the model must not have seen.

benchmarks.name: vi-overrefusal
benchmarks.pending: Version 1.0 is 24 pairs and lives in ngai rather than on the Hub. It gets a revision when the set is published, and it grows by somebody writing pairs rather than by a run finishing.
benchmarks.source: built by gao, doc 10 section 1.2
benchmarks.note: Paired Vietnamese prompts: every legitimate question that safety trained models commonly refuse has a harmful twin on the same topic in the same words, so over refusal and harm refusal come off one set. Written for this benchmark, so any overlap is a leak of the benchmark itself.

benchmarks.name: vi-adherence
benchmarks.pending: Version 1.0 is 24 items and lives in theo rather than on the Hub. It gets a revision when the set is published, and it grows by somebody writing prompts rather than by a run finishing.
benchmarks.source: built by gao, doc 10 section 1.2
benchmarks.note: Vietnamese prompts with no language instruction, arranged by the shape of prompt that produces drift rather than by subject, plus items that ask for English so the set is not passed by a model that never writes it. Written for this benchmark, so any overlap is a leak of the benchmark itself.
